sentences.text: It is submitted by Shri Navneet Shukla, learned counsel for the appellant that the learned Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence on record in a proper manner.
It is pointed out that prosecutrix is a consenting adult.
Her date of birth is doubtful.
The prosecution did not produce the first school admission register so to camouflage the actual date of birth of the prosecutrix.
It is submitted that even DNA report (Ex.P/24) is low partial uninterpretable and, therefore, it could not be matched with the blood sample of the appellant.
Ex.P/25-C reveals that the prosecutrix was given admission after passing VIIIth class in the said school from where the said exhibit has been issued and proved by PW-14-B.R. Kalbhor.

Transfer Certificate is Ex.P/26-C but these documents will not take place of the first school admission register, which is the requirement of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. 5 .

Kalbhor admitted that prosecutrix had taken admission in VIth Class on 16.06.2015.
Her date of birth was recorded as 18.04.2004 on the basis of Transfer Certificate (Ex.P/26-C).
He admitted that he cannot say as to on what basis the date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned in the Transfer Certificate.
He further stated that only primary school where she had taken admission can say as to on what basis her date of birth was recorded.
6 . It is further submitted that P.W.12 is real uncle of the prosecutrix.
He has stated in paragraphs 5 & 6 of his cross-examination that his marriage was performed in the year 1995.
His brother was married after 1-2 years of his marriage.
That means father of the prosecutrix P.W.3 was married in the year 1997.
Then he admits that prosecutrix is the eldest and first child of his brother.
He further admits that birth of the first child of his brother had taken place within one and half years of the marriage.
Therefore, when tested, then date of birth of the prosecutrix will be of the year 1999.
He further admitted that the prosecutrix was married a year back.
He further admits that the marriage of a girl is performed only when she completes 18 years of age.
Thus, it is submitted that the prosecutrix was major at the time of the incident.
This witness admitted that his age is about 50 years.
7. Reading from the evidence of the lady doctor P.W.7- Dr. Monika Soni, she opined that she had examined the prosecutrix on 05.12.2018 at District Hospital, Betul.

8. Shri Nitin Kumar Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor, in his turn, supports the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence and submits that no interference is called for in the same.
9. P.W.2 - Prosecutrix admitted that she had gone to Delhi.
She admits that she has no document in regard to her date of birth.
She also admits that she had gone to Delhi by train.

She further admits that there are several houses close to her house and if she would have raised an alarm, then that could have reached to the neighbours so also to the Aanganwadi Center, which is adjacent to her house.
She admitted that on the date of the incident, she had not narrated her story either to her parents or any other person.
She further admitted that she had not given any statement to the police personnel and had given her version to her parents on return from Delhi.
In paragraph 7 of her cross-examination, she admits that she was giving her statements as being tutored by a lady advocate.
10. P.W.3 father of the prosecutrix admitted that he had seen the incident and thereafter lodged missing person report.
This is a contradictory statement.

If he had seen the incident taking place,
then there was no occasion for him to lodge a missing person report, but should have recorded FIR straightaway saying that his minor daughter's privacy was violated.
He admitted that after one and a half month of the incident, the prosecutrix had called him and informed him that she was in Bombay.
He had found the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30667 5 CRA-282-2023 prosecutrix sitting on the bank of river Tapti when he had taken her to the police station.
In cross-examination, this witness admits that he is illiterate.
This witness further admits that after prosecutrix ran away, he neither had any communication with the girl nor he had informed anything about the incident to his wife.
After having said that he had narrated the story to the relatives and the Sarpanch, he changed his stand and stated that he had not narrated anything to anybody as people indulge in mudslinging.

11 . When evidence of P.W.2 prosecutrix, P.W.3 father of the prosecutrix, P.W.7 - Dr. Monika Soni, P.W.12 - uncle of the prosecutrix and P.W.14- B.R.Kalbhor is read holistically, then it is evident that there is no mention of the fact that the prosecutrix was kidnapped by the appellant.
When P.W.3 father of the prosecutrix had witnessed the incident and appellant was known to him, then he should have lodged an FIR rather than lodging missing person report against unknown person.
12. Prosecutrix's absconding for about two months reflects her consent.
She did not reveal her story to anybody for a long duration of two months.
P.W.7 - Dr. Monika Soni found no external or internal injury marks on her body.
P.W.12 - real uncle of the prosecutrix has through chronological analysis established that the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
Her date of birth will be of the year 1991.
When all these facts are taken into consideration, then it cannot be said that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident.
